A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, models, core equations and experiments. All pages are readable, including v3's Appendices A–G. V4 ends after its references and incorporates selected appendix material into the main text, allowing relocation to be distinguished from omission.

before.justification: V3 reports original token-alignment measurements, spectral analyses, sparse-retrieval results and interpretability examples, with additional experiments in Appendices E–G.

after.justification: V4 retains original alignment and spectral results in Figures 2–4, sparse-retrieval results in Table 3, and interpretability examples in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The token-projection and ranking procedure, first-principal-component adjustment, and sparse document/query construction remain unchanged. V4's Algorithm 1 reproduces Process 1 from v3 Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both retain Wikipedia alignment evaluation, report similar findings on SNLI and MS MARCO, and evaluate retrieval on FiQA, NFCorpus, SciFact and ArguAna. Both interpretability scenarios remain. Missing supplementary measurements and linguistic analyses reduce supporting evidence without establishing changed benchmark or application-task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Appendix A explicitly includes GTE among models tested in preliminary alignment checks; v4's corresponding Section 6 omits this qualitative comparator. The eight principal embedders and their backbones remain, as do BM25 and SPLADEv2 in Table 3.

E3.justification: V4 removes Appendix G.3's distinct evaluation procedure using 500 MS MARCO query-document pairs, top-five aligned-token matching and spaCy linguistic annotations. The retained experiments preserve the stated 10K-Wikipedia setup, alignment metrics, nDCG@10 and K/M search ranges; no revision or rerun of these protocols is established.

E4.justification: V4 omits the detailed K/M sensitivity curves, cross-dataset alignment checks and examples, first-component interventions for OPT/LLaMA/Mistral, and the parent-word linguistic analysis from v3 Appendices E–G. General summaries survive for several omitted analyses. The eight-model spectral comparison and semantic-relatedness example are retained through relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. V3's hyperparameter curves describe different settings rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Under the same stated setup, Figure 2 changes LLM2Vec's plotted Hit@10/LAR/GAR from approximately 0.975/0.124/0.268 to 0.999/0.198/0.377, without explaining why. V4 also removes the substantial result sets in v3 Figures 6–9 and Table 8. Table 3's retrieval scores, all eight relocated spectral plots, and the retained interpretability-example values are unchanged.

T1.justification: V4 removes Appendix E.4's dense-versus-sparse FLOP derivation, including the ratio (Mhat + K)/(2d) and its numerical substitution. The core alignment definitions and spectral reasoning in Equations 1–16 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: broadly observed key-token alignment, dominant first-component changes, sparse retrieval retaining about 80% of dense performance, and interpretability applications. Moving supporting material into the main text does not expand these claims.

C2.justification: V4 drops the Platonic Representation Hypothesis rationale for LLaMAEOL's anomalous behavior and the qualification that estimated retrieval overhead depends on chunk/index settings. Section 5.2 describes the same aligned tokens as positive/negative emotions rather than joy/sadness. The principal English-only, encoder-only-model and first-component limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code-repository link but removes exact checkpoint and LoRA access information from Appendix B. It also removes Appendix E's BEIR source, dataset statistics, retrieval instructions, test-set sweep disclosure, software versions and A100 40GB/CUDA setup. These are substantial documentation losses, without evidence that the underlying retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: V4 adds Abdalla et al. (2023) on semantic relatedness and removes references including Huh et al. (2024), GTE, DPR, MPNet, Spider and MNLI. Appendix A becomes a condensed Section 6, preserving the main distinctions from embedding inversion methods and Ram et al. (2023).

P1.justification: V4 substantially reorganizes existing content: Appendix C becomes Algorithm 1 in Section 3.2, Appendix D becomes Section 5.3, Appendix A becomes Section 6, and part of Appendix F enters Section 4. Remaining appendix sections disappear, alongside copyediting and terminology changes. Section 4 still refers to four pairs although Figure 3 now shows eight.

P2.justification: V4 merges v3 Figures 3 and 5 into one eight-panel Figure 3 and relocates Figure 4, Table 5 and the algorithm display. V3 Figures 6–9 and Tables 6–8 are omitted. These substantially change the displayed evidence and its organization.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially weakens support and reproducibility for its retained generality, first-component and efficiency claims. It removes cross-dataset measurements, additional backbone interventions, sensitivity curves, FLOP assumptions, exact checkpoints and retrieval prompts. Integrating retained material into the main text and adding a code link improve accessibility, but these gains do not compensate for the loss of important supporting evidence and documentation in the supplied paper.
